metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted values by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days post-spike.
- After a significant price drop, model tends to underestimate the subsequent rebound; add 3–8% upward bias in the 10–15 day window following a dip.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias toward historical averages; adjust forecasts to align with 18-day rolling mean if no event-driven sentiment.
- Overshoots after spikes are common in the 10–20 day horizon; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 10–15% in the 15–25 day window after a peak.
- If no official event context is present, model overweights recent volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to recent 3-day moves by using 18-day weighted average instead of 7-day moving average.
